gland.def: One cell or a group of epithelial cells that makes a product and releases it (secretion).

exocrine-gland.def: A gland whose product travels through a duct, or for a single-cell gland directly, onto a surface such as the skin or the inside of the gut. A serous gland releases watery, enzyme-rich fluid; a mucous gland releases mucus.

endocrine-gland.def: A ductless gland that releases hormones into the interstitial fluid, from where they diffuse into capillaries and travel in the blood to target cells.

secretion-modes.def: The three ways an exocrine cell releases its product: merocrine (by exocytosis; the cell stays whole), apocrine (the product-filled apical end pinches off) and holocrine (the whole cell breaks apart and becomes the secretion).
